To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Polish government was able to improve the transposition record of its ministries by extending stricter rules that constrained the discretion of ministers and their departments to act in a self-interested manner.

the Polish government’s pre-accession transposition record was positively influenced by the configuration and institutionalization of core executive rules that the government could use to extend select incentives and monitoring to the line ministers and their staff.
the Polish government was successful in improving the transposition record of its line ministries in the period 1997- 2002.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of how and why the Polish government's record of transposing European Community law changed between 1997 and 2002, a period of time that covers the last three years before the accession of Poland to the European Union.
the role that the core executive institutions play in the process of Europeanization.
the transposition of European Community legislation in the new member states.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the core executive institutions in Poland were instrumental in the Europeanization of the country's domestic policy-making process.
the core executive was the most important factor in explaining the variation in the transposition record over the period under review.
the Polish core executive institutions played a crucial role in the transposition process and that the effect of core executive rules on transposition depended on other variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the core executive is a crucial factor in explaining the transposition record in new EU member states.
this thesis shows how the core executive institutions can shape the transposition record in Poland.

the core executive institutions in Poland have been a crucial factor in the transposition of EC law prior to accession, and that the impact of the core executive institutions has been conditioned by EU incentives and the political context.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Europeanization of public policies is not only a function of EU incentives and domestic political factors, but is also decisively influenced by national executive rules and the ability of the national government to use these rules to shape the behaviour of line ministries.
the transposition record of the new member states can be improved by strengthening the control mechanisms of the domestic core executive vis-a vis the line ministries.
the core executive's capacity to influence the transposition of European Community legislation is not a given but a product of its own institutionalization.
